summary: Keepalive churn after 1.4.0 client library upgrade results in tenant-wide 429 surge
description:
Issue summary: After BrightLens upgraded their Redwood client SDK from v1.3.9 to v1.4.0, they observed a sudden wave of 429 responses across their tenant in us-east. Impact: Production ingestion pipelines and real-time chat features saw repeated 429s for ~18 minutes, causing partial data loss for a subset of background workers and elevated error rates for interactive sessions.

Observed behavior: Tenant-level token quotas were exhausted quickly with many short-lived keepalive/healthcheck requests counted against burst credits. The 429s present as opaque rejections (no explicit route-level exhaustion metadata) and coincide with spikes in connection churn from the customer's side after the client upgrade.

Expected behavior: The client upgrade should not materially increase keepalive frequency or cause double-counting. Background heartbeats and short-lived connection probes should be excluded from burst credit accounting when the customer's recommended keepalive exemption flag is active.

Customer note: Customer has flagged that only client SDKs were changed, no server-side config or deployment changes. They attached SDK logs and said backoff logic is standard, but observed retries escalate rapidly when 429s start.

Links:
- Support thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C_SUPPORT/p1646001234000
- Dashboard (rate limiter / tenant): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/tenant/brightlens/rate-limiter?from=2026-03-10T02:00Z&to=2026-03-10T02:30Z
- Customer-provided SDK logs: s3://support-uploads/brightlens/sdklogs/2026-03-10-keepalive.zip
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Upgrade Redwood client SDK from v1.3.9 to v1.4.0 using pip/npm package
2) Start a fleet of lightweight background workers (50-100) configured with default keepalive/healthcheck=enabled
3) Observe connection churn during deploy (workers reconnecting while upgrade rolls out),
4) Monitor /v1/usage and tenant token buckets for burst depletion and 429 responses
logs:
Edge logs (snippet): 2026-03-10T02:07:12Z tenant=brightlens conn_id=abc123 KEEPALIVE start
Rate limiter trace: token_bucket_refill: window=60s refill=1000 consumed=1180 (spike)
Customer SDK sample: reconnect loop delayed backoff 200ms -> 400ms -> 800ms then parallel restart of 40 workers
comments: 2026-03-10 02:25 - Support (Aisha Patel): Customer reports 18 minute spike starting 02:05 UTC, all interactive endpoints showed elevated 429. Requesting immediate guidance and whether this is expected after client upgrade.

2026-03-10 02:40 - SRE (Daniel Kim): Triage started. Initial rate-limiter graphs show tenant token depletion coincident with ~600 short-lived keepalive requests/min. Investigating whether keepalive subjects are being counted as standard requests rather than 'probe' category.

2026-03-10 03:05 - Eng (Rita Sanchez): Noted client SDK change log includes a socket reconnect batching optimization that may cause simultaneous reconnects when process restarts. Flagging a potential throttling amplification. Creating an instrumentation branch to correlate connection IDs.

2026-03-11 10:12 - Support (Aisha Patel): Customer confirmed they temporarily rolled back to client v1.3.9 and the 429 waves stopped. They can reproduce on staging with v1.4.0 under a rolling deploy pattern.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: v1.4.0 introduced synchronous reconnect behavior on startup that causes keepalives to fire earlier and in aggregate, pushing tenant over burst window.
Hypothesis 2: Edge proxy now counts certain preflight/keepalive frames as full tokens due to header changes in the new SDK (SNI/host header difference).
Data: Correlated edge metrics (conn churn vs token consumption) show a 7x increase in connection open/close rate for the customer's tenant during rollout period.
Checked linked rate-limiter config: tenant has default burst pool with 60s window, no exempted probe pool configured for this tenant.
resolution_notes: Workaround (short-term): Advise customer to roll back to v1.3.9 or apply staged rollout with randomized reconnect jitter. They rolled back and observed normal behavior within 4 minutes.
Mitigation (platform): Engineering to add a temporary rule to classify rapid keepalive/healthcheck patterns from this tenant as 'probe' for 24h to prevent burst depletion while SDK fix is delivered.

Permanent fix (follow-up): Client SDK team to patch v1.4.1 to add randomized reconnect jitter and avoid synchronous heartbeat emission. Edge team to validate header normalization so probe frames are not token-accounted when probe-exemption header is present.
Rollout plan: feature flag gp/keepalive-exempt for edge to be deployed canary to us-east by 2026-03-15. SDK patch expected CI->release by 2026-03-14.
